$comment: Real-binary evidence ledger for the tunnel methods (TASK-65).
scripts/test-method-matrix.ts runs each method with an INJECTED process
handle and cannot execute a tunnel binary, so it reports realBinary:false
for every method by construction. That is honest about the harness but it
cannot see real-binary runs performed OUTSIDE the harness.
This file is the input that lets the matrix report what was actually proved:
an entry may only exist when a real tunnel binary was executed on the target
OS and real bytes crossed the tunnel. Everything not listed stays false.

runs.binaryVersion: pingtunnel 2.10 (git d225084), upstream release asset esrrhs/pingtunnel 2.10
runs.target: xt24, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS x86_64, systemd PID 1 (privileged container), uid 0 with CAP_NET_RAW; two network namespaces (ns-cli / ns-srv) joined by a veth link, because pingtunnel 2.10 panics at server.go:357 when both halves share one loopback address
runs.configSource: scripts/test-real-icmp-tunnel.sh -> the product's own builder (buildIcmpServerConfig / buildIcmpClientConfig from packages/tunnel-core/src/config/pingtunnel.js), mode 0600, invoked as `pingtunnel -c <config>` so the key and passphrase never reach argv
checks: the product's builder produced both node configs (0700 dir, 0600 files)
the shared AES-256 passphrase is inside both configs and absent from argv
raw ICMP echo between the two nodes answered before any tunnel existed
the backend answered on the FOREIGN node as a pre-tunnel baseline
carried real TCP bytes across the ICMP hop: ns-cli:18108 -> FOREIGN -> :18109 returned the backend body HELLO-ICMP
both halves logged real ICMP traffic and neither crashed while carrying it
both halves still running after the transfer
the generated systemd unit runs pingtunnel as root and opens its raw ICMP socket with no permission error (scripts/test-icmp-systemd-unit.sh: 4/4)
runs.reconnectNote: not claimed: this suite proves a single continuous transfer, not that the tunnel recovers after a restart
runs.evidenceNote: scripts/test-real-icmp-tunnel.sh on xt24: 14 passed, 0 failed across 4 consecutive runs, plus scripts/test-icmp-systemd-unit.sh: 4 passed, 0 failed (User=root mutation fails it). Mutation: removing the client half (no ICMP bridge) fails the transfer check (12 passed, 2 failed), so the pass is not vacuous. Limits: the hop is a veth link inside one container, so this proves ICMP raw-socket transport end to end between two real nodes but NOT that a given internet path permits ping. SOCKS5 mode and UDP forwarding remain untested. The systemd privilege path IS now proven: scripts/test-icmp-systemd-unit.sh starts the exact unit buildUnit() emits and confirms pingtunnel runs as root and opens its raw socket (4/4; mutating User=root to User=nobody fails it).

methodsWithoutRealBinaryEvidence.reason: Metadata-only by design: X-UI records the status of a third-party 3x-ui panel and runs no tunnel binary on our nodes, so there is no binary to execute. Status is established by a real panel verification instead. Not a coverage gap: PRD.md:112 specifies XUI's requirements as private-network exception, credential-free sync payload, API failure behavior and bounded retries -- none of which is a tunnel binary. Those four are asserted in scripts/test-xui.ts (61 passed, 0 failed). This field records which methods run an Xistance engine, which is a different question from which methods meet their PRD requirements.

note: Real-binary coverage is 8/9. Only XUI is listed without real-binary evidence, and it is metadata-only by design rather than blocked by the environment. Validated by scripts/test-real-binary-evidence.ts, which requires the two lists to be an exact partition of the nine methods and requires an explicit reason for every unproved entry.
